A: Hi, yeah, I can hear you. Erm, can you hear me? Sorry, my internet's been funny.
B: Loud and clear. I'm Neil, I'm in Shipley, just outside Bradford.
A: I'm Sana, I'm in Luton. Nice to meet you.
B: You too. Is this your third one? I've done two and I'm getting the hang of it now. You just sort of chat, don't you?
A: Yeah, third. I was really nervous for the first one, like, what do I say? But it's been nice actually.
B: It has. So what do you do in Luton, Sana?
A: Erm, I'm job-hunting at the minute. I was a nursery practitioner, but the nursery closed down, so I'm applying for nursery jobs, school, teaching assistant, that kind of thing.
B: Oh, that's rotten luck, the place closing. Did you enjoy it?
A: I loved it. The kids, like, more than the paperwork. I did the paperwork, just sometimes last minute, lol.
B: Ha, that's most people. I'm a lab technician at a university, so I'm the bloke who makes sure the fume cupboards work. But honestly, half my job's the same as yours. Some first-year comes in panicking because their practical's gone wrong, and you just sort of calm them down and explain it again without making them feel daft.
A: That's literally a nursery, just bigger kids.
B: Bigger kids with Bunsen burners. That's the worrying bit.
A: Lol. Erm, I've thought about doing SEN teaching assistant, or even early years teacher one day, but I don't know if I'm clever enough for a degree, you know?
B: Can I say summat? I didn't do a degree. I did an HNC part-time while I was working, in me twenties, and I thought I'd be found out every week. Turned out it's mostly turning up and asking questions. And if you can calm a room full of three-year-olds, you're more qualified than you think.
A: Aww, thank you. That's really nice. I did start an access course once but I stopped when I went full time.
B: Well, it's still there, isn't it? It doesn't go anywhere.
A: Yeah, true. What do you do outside work, then?
B: Walking, mostly. I did Ilkley Moor in the rain last weekend and came back like a drowned rat. And I sing in a choir, bass. We're doing the Christmas stuff already.
A: Already? It's not even, like, near Christmas.
B: Tell that to our conductor. What about you?
A: I do mehndi, henna, for weddings. Brides, cousins, that kind of thing. I've got a booking next month.
B: Oh, that's a proper skill, that. Steady hands. I can barely label a sample bottle neatly.
A: It takes ages though. A bride's hands can be like four hours.
B: Four hours! Do they have to sit still the whole time?
A: They try. Their aunties keep feeding them, lol.
B: Sounds like a decent deal to me. Do you cook as well? I'm always asking people that, sorry, it's a bit of an obsession.
A: Yeah, most evenings. Karahi, daal, rotis, but my rotis are never round, my mum always says. And I tried an air fryer recipe yesterday and it went so wrong. It was meant to be crispy and it was just, like, sad.
B: Ha! I do tea for me mam and dad most nights, but on Saturdays I have a go at curry from scratch. Bradford's spoiled me, mind, I've got a lot to live up to.
